Marcus —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are moving forward with a reserved capacity commitment (proposal attached to Diego) and need Redwood to validate sizing and provide a cutover timeline so we can align internal approvals. High-level asks:

- Confirm GPU count and instance mix required for steady-state 1.8k qps peak (text-generation workload, avg 28 tokens per request).
- Acceptance tests we should run (throughput, tail latency at 99.9th).
- Suggested rehearsal/cutover windows and blackout periods (we prefer weeknights but are flexible).
- Any recommended quantization or model variant tradeoffs to reduce cost while meeting latency SLOs.

Attached: nucleus_traffic_profile.csv (hourly) and proj_scope.pdf (SOW).

Can you kick off a sizing validation and propose a timeline? Diego and I are aiming for a hard launch week of 2027-11-08 if feasible.

Best,
Aisha

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 29 Oct 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted->Dedicated migration: request for sizing validation and timeline

Thanks Marcus — drafted a technical sizing assessment based on the supplied profile. Key points (draft):

- Workload assumptions: peak concurrency ~1800 qps, average prompt+completion = 28 tokens (approx 175 total tokens/sec aggregate).
- Candidate model: rdx-open-4b-approx (we suggest running QoE eval vs one larger variant in staging).
- Execution profile: target p99 latency <= 250ms, p99.9 <= 450ms with CPU-managed batching disabled for tail-sensitive endpoints.

Sizing sketch (initial):
- 8x A100-80GB pods with 16 concurrent requests per pod using dynamic batching (batch target 32) — estimated steady-state throughput ~2.2k qps headroom.
- Fallback: 12x A100-80GB pods for heavy-day burst / failover.
- Cost option: quantize to int8 and reduce to 6x A100-80GB for non-tail traffic; requires acceptance test for regression.

Acceptance tests we need you to run in staging (we can run them with you):
1) Step-load to peak and hold 30min. Verify token throughput and p99/p99.9.
2) Intermittent burst test with synthetic 2x peak for 10 minutes to verify fallback routing.
3) Regression prompt set run before/after quantization to check quality drift (<3% delta L1).

Timing constraints: to meet 11/08 launch, we need to complete sizing validation and a full swap rehearsal by 11/04 EOD. That gives Ops two nights for the final swap window (11/05–11/06).

I’ll prepare a sizing_matrix.xlsx (draft) and drop it into the shared Drive. Questions / deviations please flag.

—Neha
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — Ops notes and proposed cutover cadence below. I’ll own the swap orchestration and provide runbooks.

Proposed Cadence (operational):
- 11/02–11/03: Staging stress validation (Neha + Nucleus). Smoke tests and regression harness.
- 11/04 (night): Dry-run swap to a shadow reserved fleet (no traffic cut). Verify routing, KV cache warm, monitor tail latencies.
- 11/05 (night): Primary swap — 00:30–02:30 PT low-traffic window. Plan: gradual traffic ramp (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) with 15-min hold at each step. Rollback criteria pre-defined.
- 11/06: Post-swap monitoring and throttled scale-down of fallbacks.

Pre-reqs from Nucleus: signed commitment (deal id NCL-7281), point-of-contact on call during swap (ops lead + PM), and acceptance-test signoff after staging.

I’ll create the orchestration runbook and share a Drive link. Also adding the HubSpot deal to the ops calendar and creating a Jira ticket: SUP-4889.

—Jonas
